oewn-05127416-n.learner: a very great amount of something, far more than is needed
examples: The market offered an embarrassment of fresh fruit, more than we could ever eat.

oewn-06279437-n.learner: a special or important article in a newspaper or magazine
examples: The magazine ran a long feature on young farmers.

oewn-03330714-n.learner: a product that a shop shows or advertises more than its other products
examples: This week's feature at the shop is a cheap coffee maker, placed right by the door.

oewn-05858739-n.learner: in the study of language, a special quality of a sound, word, or other unit that makes it different from other units of the same kind
examples: Voicing is the feature that separates the sound 'b' from the sound 'p'.
He slept little the night before the exam.

oewn-05799460-n.learner: the right or the chance to choose
examples: If I had my preference, we would eat outside tonight.

oewn-02431950-v.learner: to set up or found something so that it begins to exist
examples: The school was established by a group of parents in 1850.

oewn-01650771-v.learner: to set something up, or to prepare the ground for it
examples: The company plans to establish a new department next year.

oewn-00667394-v.learner: to bring in, pass, or set up something such as a rule or law
examples: The council established a new rule about parking in the town centre.

oewn-01651214-v.learner: to make something happen or come to exist
examples: The treaty established peace between the two countries.

oewn-00638550-v.learner: to use something as the base that something else stands on
examples: She established her argument on a careful study of the facts.

oewn-01766380-v.learner: to make someone upset, excited, or stirred up
examples: The loud thunder excited the horses, and they ran around the field.

oewn-00504245-v.learner: to work as a stimulant, making the body or mind more active
examples: Coffee excites the nervous system and keeps you awake.

oewn-01766135-v.learner: to make someone feel sexual desire
examples: Some perfumes are made to excite a partner sexually.

oewn-00560179-v.learner: to raise something to a higher level of energy
examples: Light from the lamp can excite the atoms in the gas.

oewn-00560040-v.learner: to make a magnetic field in something
examples: An electric current is used to excite the coils of the motor.

oewn-01048915-a.learner: (of speech or writing) following the traditional rules of correct language, without casual words, short forms, or everyday expressions
examples: Use formal English when you write a letter to the bank.

oewn-01987861-s.learner: shown in a simple form or by using symbols
examples: The artist drew the trees in a formal way, as plain green triangles.

oewn-01433501-s.learner: worked out by logical reasoning, step by step from what is already known
examples: She wrote a formal proof of the theorem.

oewn-06315049-n.learner: the set of words used to name things in a particular subject or field of work
examples: The language of medicine can be hard for patients to understand.

oewn-05816565-n.learner: the mental processes we use to make and understand speech and writing
examples: He didn't have the language to express his feelings.

oewn-07066015-n.learner: the words of a popular song or of a song in a musical comedy
examples: The language of the song is simple enough for children to sing along.

oewn-02654741-v.learner: to live in a certain place
examples: The same family has occupied the old farmhouse for twenty years.

oewn-02399325-v.learner: to take on a position or role
examples: The young prince will soon occupy the throne.
Thoughts of her sick mother occupied her all through the journey.

oewn-02655144-v.learner: to fill the whole of something
examples: The crowd occupied every seat in the hall.

oewn-01128786-v.learner: to march with an army into another country's land in order to conquer it and hold it
examples: Enemy troops occupied the northern towns within a week.

oewn-02609063-v.learner: to bring people or groups together for a shared purpose, action, or belief, or in a shared situation
examples: The threat of war united the whole country.
The small drops of water united into one large drop.

oewn-02637244-v.learner: to have two or more qualities or things together at the same time
examples: I never saw such capacity, and taste, and application, and elegance, as you describe, united.
